Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13          Pending before the Court is Defendant’s motion to dismiss Plaintiffs’ consolidated
                                  14   complaint. See Dkt. No. 65 (“Mot.”); Dkt. No. 68 (“Opp.”); Dkt. No. 71 (“Reply”). The Court
                                  15   finds this matter appropriate for disposition without oral argument and the matter is deemed
                                  16   submitted. See Civil L.R. 7-1(b). The Court GRANTS the motion to dismiss.
                                  17          In August 2025, Plaintiffs Ranfis Espinal Aguilera, Jason Demmie, Alfredo Diaz, Deborah
                                  18   Finley, Marcus Hines, Stevie Newson, and Randall Wright filed a consolidated class action
                                  19   complaint against Defendant Smart ERP Solutions, Inc. alleging that Defendant failed to
                                  20   safeguard class members’ sensitive personally identifying information, which was stolen during a
                                  21   data breach. See Dkt. No. 57 (“Compl.”) ¶¶ 1–2. Plaintiffs bring state law claims on behalf of a
                                  22   nationwide class for negligence, unjust enrichment, and breach of third-party beneficiary
                                  23   contracts. Id. ¶¶ 214–259.
                                  24          Defendant argues that the Court should dismiss all three claims because Plaintiffs have not
                                  25   identified which substantive state law applies to their claims. Mot. at 12. The Court agrees.
                                  26   Courts in this district routinely hold that “due to variances among state laws, failure to allege
                                  27   which state law governs a common law claim is grounds for dismissal.” In re Nexus 6P Prods.
                                  28   Liab. Litig., 293 F. Supp. 3d 888, 933 (N.D. Cal. 2018) (quotation omitted); Moore v. Am. Honda
                                            Case 4:25-cv-02588-HSG        Document 77       Filed 02/25/26      Page 2 of 3




                                   1   Motor Co., 740 F. Supp. 3d 814, 829 (N.D. Cal. 2024) (same). “In order for the Court to

                                   2   determine whether a claim has been adequately pled, Plaintiff[s] must allege the applicable law.”

                                   3   Moore, 740 F. Supp. 3d at 829.1

                                   4           Plaintiffs argue that California law applies, Opp. at 11–12, citing Mazza v. American

                                   5   Honda Motor Co., 666 F.3d 581 (9th Cir. 2012), overruled by Olean Wholesale Grocery

                                   6   Cooperative, Inc. v. Bumble Bee Foods LLC, 31 F.4th 651 (9th Cir. 2022). But Mazza explains

                                   7   when California law may be used on a classwide basis for a multistate class, id. at 590, and it does

                                   8   not eliminate the initial pleading requirements discussed here, cf. Romero v. Flowers Bakeries,

                                   9   LLC, No. 14-CV-05189-BLF, 2016 WL 469370, at *12 (N.D. Cal. Feb. 8, 2016) (noting that a

                                  10   similar argument “considers not whether a plaintiff needs to assert the state law under which s/he

                                  11   brings a common law claim, but rather whether, given the chosen state, a nationwide class is

                                  12   appropriate”).2
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13           Accordingly, Defendant’s motion to dismiss, Dkt. No. 65, is GRANTED with leave to

                                  14   amend. Lopez v. Smith, 203 F.3d 1122, 1127 (9th Cir. 2000) (en banc) (noting that the “court

                                  15   should grant leave to amend even if no request to amend the pleading was made, unless it

                                  16   determines that the pleading could not possibly be cured by the allegation of other facts”

                                  17   (quotation omitted)). Any amended complaint must be filed within 21 days of the date of this

                                  18   order, and may not add any new claims or defendants.

                                  19           //

                                  20           //

                                  21

                                  22   1
                                        For example, the Court needs to know which state laws apply when considering Defendant’s
                                  23   argument that failure to comply with Section 5 of the FTC Act—which does not provide for a
                                       private right of action—does not constitute negligence per se. Mot. at 14. Plaintiffs cite a handful
                                  24   of states’ different approaches, Opp. at 13–14, forcing the Court and Defendant to try and guess
                                       which applies and respond to them all. In this way, the requirement that a plaintiff plead the
                                  25   applicable state law also serves an essential notice function.
                                       2
                                  26     The Court also notes that many of Plaintiffs’ cited cases included more specific allegations that
                                       tied the alleged conduct to the location of the defendant’s headquarters. See Opp. at 12. Here, it’s
                                  27   not a surprise that Defendant was unsure about what state’s laws to apply, since Plaintiffs mention
                                       California only once in their complaint, and none of the named Plaintiffs reside in California.
                                  28   Compl. ¶ 23 (“Defendant is a California corporation . . . .”), ¶¶ 16–22 (discussing named
                                       Plaintiffs).
                                                                                          2
                                         Case 4:25-cv-02588-HSG   Document 77       Filed 02/25/26   Page 3 of 3
